These accesses crash or yield undefined whenever CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, breaking every token refresh for those integrations. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the Hubspot, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM and Google callers expect provider-specific shapes (hubspot client object with fields, axios response with `.data`, google `{res:{data}}`). When CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, hubspot's `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token`, zoho's `tokenInfo.data.error`, and google's `res?.data` all read undefined/throw TypeError on a fetch Response (which has no `.data`), crashing every booking that touches those integrations instead of refreshing tokens.

adjudication.rationale: In sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch(...)` Response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Multiple callers still treat the return value as a provider/axios/google client result: GoogleCalendarService does `const token = res?.data` (expects an axios-like `{data}`) (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), Hubspot types the return as `HubspotToken` and will read token fields (packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts), and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM access `tokenInfo.data...` / `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data...` (expects axios response) (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts). A fetch Response has no `.data` and does not directly expose token fields, so these paths will yield undefined and/or throw, breaking token refresh in sharing mode.
